options: Converts a natural-language business question into SQL, runs it, and returns both the data and the generated SQL
Replaces the need for any Snowflake tables or warehouses
Only generates SQL text without ever executing it
Translates SQL into natural language, the reverse of its actual purpose
questions.explain: Cortex Analyst generates SQL from a plain-English question, executes it, and shows both the result and the SQL that produced it.

questions.q: What does Cortex Analyst reason against to generate accurate SQL, rather than guessing from raw table/column names?
options: A semantic model — a YAML file mapping business vocabulary to tables, dimensions, measures, and synonyms
A random sample of unrelated tables
The Snowflake account's billing history
A fixed list of SQL keywords with no table information at all
questions.explain: The semantic model is the grounding contract: it names the real tables/columns behind business terms and can include verified question/SQL pairs.

questions.q: Under which role does the SQL generated by Cortex Analyst execute?
options: The asking user's own role, so existing RBAC, masking, and row-access policies still apply
A shared service account with full ACCOUNTADMIN privileges
No role at all — it bypasses Snowflake's security model entirely
The role of whoever created the semantic model, regardless of who asks the question
questions.explain: Cortex Analyst's generated SQL runs as the asking user, so it can't surface data that user's role couldn't already query directly.

questions.q: What does a 'verified query' in a semantic model provide?
options: A known-good question/SQL pair that anchors the model's accuracy for common questions
A query that has been encrypted for security purposes
A query that only an administrator is allowed to run
A randomly generated SQL statement used for load testing
questions.explain: Verified queries pair a real natural-language question with correct, known-good SQL, improving accuracy for similar future questions.

questions.q: According to this lesson's 2026 update, how has Cortex Analyst's role been evolving?
options: Snowflake has been shifting SQL generation into Cortex Agents, where a semantic view is used directly as an agent tool, improving accuracy and latency
Cortex Analyst has been completely removed from Snowflake with no replacement
Cortex Analyst now requires a separate third-party LLM provider
Semantic models are no longer used anywhere in Snowflake's AI stack
questions.explain: Snowflake's 2026 release notes recommend transitioning from the standalone Cortex Analyst API toward Cortex Agents using a semantic view as a tool, which generates SQL directly inside the agent loop.
